mainTopic: Why borrowing and buying are forbidden in the earlier משנה, the vow about a neighbor's cow, indirect ways to help a hungry מודר, and רבי יוסי's view of הפקר
overview: The גמרא first asks about the previous משנה. If only one person is forbidden to benefit from the other, why can't the other person borrow money, borrow an object or buy from him, since that seems to give him nothing? רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers that both people vowed against each other. אביי answers that the חכמים made a גזירה: borrowing from him may lead to lending to him. A new משנה follows. A man who is refused a cow vows that plowing his field with it is a קונם, and how far the vow reaches depends on whether he usually plows himself. The משנה then shows ways to help a hungry מודר without giving to him directly: hinting to a shopkeeper or to workers and paying them later, giving food as a gift to a third person, or making the food הפקר. רבי יוסי forbids the הפקר method. רבי יוחנן explains that for רבי יוסי, הפקר works like a gift and stays the owner's until someone takes it. רבי אבא challenges this from a ברייתא where רבי יוסי forbids only when the vow came before the הפקר, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why is borrowing from him forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה forbids the other person to borrow money from the מודר, since that seems to give the מודר no benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he may not lend to him, because that benefits him. But why may he not borrow from him? How does that benefit him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the previous משנה. Lending to the מודר obviously helps him, but borrowing from the מודר seems to give him nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture two people. Person A is the מודר, who is forbidden to get any benefit from Person B. When B lends to A, A clearly benefits. When B borrows from A, A is the one giving, so where is A's forbidden benefit?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, granted (sets up a contrast: 'this is fine, but...')

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two people straight. The מודר (Person A) is the one who may not benefit. The question is about B doing things for A or taking things from A.

phrases.english: Gemara: It makes sense that he may not lend to him
because he is giving him benefit.
But that he may not borrow from him,
how is he giving him benefit?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לֹא יַלְוֶנּוּ דְּקָא מַהֲנֵי לֵיהּ אֶלָּא לָא יִלְוֶה הֵימֶנּוּ מַאי קָא מַהֲנֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the previous משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the other person may not borrow from the מודר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vow against getting benefit should only forbid the מודר from receiving. When someone borrows from him, he receives nothing.

steps.title: Even harder: why is borrowing an item forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further. Borrowing money and buying might give the מודר some benefit, but borrowing an item gives him none at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if we say that borrowing money from him and buying from him are forbidden because he gets some benefit, why may he not borrow an object from him? How does he benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its question stronger. It admits there may be an answer for borrowing money and buying, but it says borrowing an object still makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When A lends money or sells something, A can gain in a small way. Lending keeps his money's value safe, and selling gets rid of an item that is hard to sell. But when A lends out an object, he just gets the same object back, so he gains nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He will borrow an object from him (to be returned as is)

steps.confusionAlert: Hebrew has two kinds of borrowing. לִלְווֹת is borrowing money, which you pay back with different coins. לִשְׁאוֹל is borrowing an object, which you return itself.

phrases.english: And granted that he may not borrow money from him
and may not buy from him,
because he does get benefit from him,
phrases.notes: The lender keeps his money's value safe, and the seller gets rid of goods that are hard to sell.

phrases.english: but that he may not borrow an object from him,
what benefit does he get from him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִשְׁלָמָא לֹא יִלְוֶה הֵימֶנּוּ וְלֹא יִקַּח הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule against borrowing an object from the מודר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if lending money or selling gives some small gain, lending out an object gives nothing back except the same object.

steps.title: Both people vowed against each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the משנה is talking about a case where each person vowed not to benefit from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: The case is where they both vowed not to benefit from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers the question by changing the case. Here both people are forbidden to benefit from each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vow goes both ways, every action that helps either side is forbidden. Borrowing and buying now help the other person, who is also a מודר, so the question disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, the case is like
This one from that one, each from the other

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
The case is where they vowed off benefit from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the questions of steps 1 and 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one person was forbidden, so borrowing from him gives him no benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both were forbidden to each other, so any benefit in either direction is forbidden.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree: borrowing may lead to lending
steps.stepSummary: אביי keeps the case as a one-way vow. He says the חכמים forbade borrowing from the מודר because it might lead to lending to him, and the same reason covers all the cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is a גזירה against borrowing, because of lending. The same גזירה applies to all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer. Even with a one-way vow, the חכמים made a גזירה against borrowing and buying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who borrow from each other usually end up lending back. If B borrows from A, B will likely lend to A one day, and that would be real forbidden benefit. So borrowing money, borrowing objects and buying are all forbidden only מדרבנן, as a fence.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree of the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says both people vowed. אביי says only one vowed, and the extra rules are a rabbinic גזירה.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is a decree against borrowing
because of lending,
phrases.notes: If you borrow from someone, you'll probably lend back to him, and that is forbidden.

phrases.english: and likewise in all of them it is a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר גְּזֵירָה לִשְׁאוֹל מִשּׁוּם לְהַשְׁאִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer instead of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Borrowing from the מודר gives him no benefit, so it should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden מדרבנן, so that it won't lead to lending to him.

steps.title: The angry vow about plowing with a neighbor's cow
steps.stepSummary: A man is refused a cow and vows that plowing his field with it is a קונם. The vow forbids only him if he plows himself, but everyone if he usually has others plow for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One man said to another: Lend me your cow. The other said: It is not free. He said: Plowing my field with it is a קונם forever. If he usually plows by himself, he is forbidden and everyone else is allowed. If he does not usually plow by himself, he and everyone else are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It shows that a vow is read according to what the person meant, based on his usual habits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he plows his own field, his words 'that I plow' mean only his own work, so others may plow for him with that cow. If others always plow for him, 'I plow' must mean his field being plowed with that cow at all. So no one may do it for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A word for making something forbidden like a קרבן
His usual way is to plow (by himself)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key rule of נדרים: we read a vow by the person's normal way of speaking and acting, not only by the bare words.

phrases.english: Mishnah: One said to another: "Lend me your cow."
He said to him: It is not available.
He said: "My field is konam,
that I plow with it, forever."
phrases.notes: He means plowing his field with that cow.

phrases.english: If his usual way was to plow himself,
he is forbidden, and all other people are permitted.
And if his usual way is not to plow himself,
he and all people are forbidden.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vow's reach depends on his habit. If he plows himself, only he is forbidden. If others plow for him, everyone is forbidden to plow his field with that cow.

steps.title: Feeding a hungry מודר through the shopkeeper
steps.stepSummary: If a מודר has nothing to eat, the other person may tell a shopkeeper about his trouble without asking directly. The shopkeeper feeds the מודר and then collects payment from the one who spoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone is forbidden by a vow to benefit from his friend and has nothing to eat, the friend goes to the shopkeeper and says: So-and-so vowed not to benefit from me, and I don't know what to do. The shopkeeper gives him food, then comes and takes payment from this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a way to help a hungry מודר. The friend hints to a shopkeeper instead of handing over food or giving a direct order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The friend never directly gives the מודר anything, and he does not even tell the shopkeeper to give. He only describes the problem. The shopkeeper decides to give on his own and later gets paid back by the friend.

keyTerms.meaning: The one forbidden by vow to benefit

steps.confusionAlert: The one who goes to the shopkeeper is not the hungry מודר. It is the friend whose benefit is forbidden to him.
steps.whatToRemember: A friend can help a מודר indirectly. He hints to a third party and does not give or command anything himself.

phrases.english: One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend
and he has nothing to eat,
goes to the shopkeeper and says:
phrases.notes: The one who goes is the friend, the one the hungry man may not benefit from.

phrases.english: So-and-so vowed off benefit from me
and I don't know what to do.
And he (the shopkeeper) gives to him,
and comes and takes payment from this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ וְאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A friend may get food to a hungry מודר indirectly. He hints to a shopkeeper and later pays him back.

steps.title: Hiring workers indirectly for the מודר
steps.stepSummary: If the מודר needs building, fencing, or harvesting done, the other person may tell workers about the situation. The workers do the job, and he pays them afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the מודר's house needed building, his fence needed putting up, or his field needed harvesting, the other person goes to the workers and says: 'So-and-so may not benefit from me, and I don't know what to do.' The workers do the job with the מודר, and then they come and take their pay from the one who spoke.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another case like the shopkeeper case. The other person helps the מודר with work by hinting to workers instead of hiring them directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as the shopkeeper case. He never directly asks the workers to work for the מודר. He only describes the trouble, and the workers choose to act on their own. Only afterward do they come and collect their pay from him.

phrases.english: If his house needed building,
phrases.notes: "His" means the מודר, the one who is not allowed to benefit.

phrases.english: his fence needed putting up,
his field needed harvesting,
he goes to the workers and says:
phrases.notes: Now "he" is the other person, the one whose things are forbidden to the מודר.

phrases.english: So-and-so is forbidden by vow to benefit from me
and I don't know what I will do.
And they do the work with him,
and they come and take pay from this one.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the person who spoke to the workers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same hinting method from the shopkeeper case to hiring workers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may hint to workers about the מודר's trouble and pay them afterward. He must not ask them directly.

steps.title: On the road, giving food through a third person
steps.stepSummary: When they travel together and the מודר has no food, the other person may give food to a third person as a real gift. The מודר may then eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were walking on the road and the מודר had nothing to eat, the other person gives food to someone else as a gift. The מודר is then allowed to eat that food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case. They are traveling and the מודר is hungry, so the food is passed through a third person by making it a full gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the food is given away, it no longer belongs to the person whose things are forbidden. It now belongs to the third person, so the מודר may eat it. The gift is what breaks the connection to the forbidden owner.

phrases.english: If they were walking on the road
and he has nothing to eat,
he gives [food] to someone else as a gift,
and that one is permitted to [eat] it.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the מודר. The food now belongs to someone else, so he may eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case of helping the מודר, this time with food while traveling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving food as a gift to a third person lets the מודר eat it.

steps.title: Making food ownerless when no one else is there
steps.stepSummary: If no third person is around, he places the food on a rock or fence and declares it ownerless, and the מודר takes it. רבי יוסי forbids this.
steps.simpleTranslation: If no one else is with them, he puts the food on a rock or a fence and says, 'These are ownerless for anyone who wants them.' The מודר then takes it and eats. רבי יוסי forbids this.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a backup plan for when there is nobody to give a gift to. The food is made ownerless (הפקר) so the מודר can take it, and the משנה ends with רבי יוסי disagreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that once the food is הפקר, it no longer belongs to the forbidden person, so the מודר may take it. רבי יוסי forbids this, but the משנה does not say why. The גמרא explains his reason next.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי argues about the gift case in the previous step. He only argues about the הפקר method.

phrases.english: If there is no one else with them,

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ עַל הַסֶּלַע אוֹ עַל הַגָּדֵר
phrases.english: he puts it on a rock or on a fence
and says: These are hereby ownerless
for anyone who wants [them],
and that one takes and eats.
And Rabbi Yosei forbids [it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a fallback for when no third person is available, and adds רבי יוסי's dissent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים allow making food הפקר for the מודר to take. רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This disagreement sets up the whole גמרא that follows, which asks how הפקר works.

steps.title: Why does רבי יוסי forbid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבי יוחנן asking for the reason behind רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יוחנן said: What is רבי יוסי's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבי יוחנן asks why רבי יוסי forbids the הפקר method, which sets up his own answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says רבי יוסי forbids. It gives no reason. This question opens the discussion of what רבי יוסי understands about how הפקר works.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara: Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dissent at the end of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רבי יוסי's ban on the הפקר method.

steps.title: הפקר works like a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that רבי יוסי compares הפקר to a gift. Just as a gift stays the giver's until it reaches the receiver, ownerless property stays the owner's until someone takes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that הפקר is like a gift. Just as a gift belongs to the giver until it passes into the receiver's hands, so too הפקר belongs to the owner until someone takes possession of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives רבי יוסי's reason: the food never left the owner's hands until the מודר picked it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, saying 'it's ownerless' does not end the ownership right away. The food stays the owner's until the taker acquires it. So when the מודר picks it up, he is taking it straight from the forbidden person, and that counts as forbidden benefit.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: for רבי יוסי, הפקר is like a gift. The owner keeps owning it until someone takes it.

phrases.english: He holds: making something ownerless is like a gift.
Just as a gift —
until it comes from the possession of the giver
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes you'll fill in: until then, it still belongs to the giver.

phrases.english: into the possession of the receiver,
so too, ownerless property —
until it comes into the possession of the one who acquires it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of רבי יוסי's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יוסי, הפקר stays the owner's until someone acquires it, just like a gift. So the מודר takes it from the forbidden owner.

steps.title: רבי אבא challenges from a ברייתא about timing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes a ברייתא where רבי יוסי forbids only when the vow came before the הפקר. This seems to clash with רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא objected: 'And that one takes and eats, and רבי יוסי forbids. רבי יוסי said: When is it forbidden? When his vow came before his making it ownerless.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא brings a ברייתא to question רבי יוחנן's explanation. In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי makes the ban depend on which came first, the vow or the הפקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי held that הפקר stays the owner's until taken, the order should not matter. Even food made ownerless before the vow would still be his, and the later vow would cover it. But the ברייתא says רבי יוסי forbids only when the vow came first, which suggests a different reason: the vow already took hold of the food.
steps.confusionAlert: The first words רבי אבא quotes sound just like our משנה. The new, challenging part is רבי יוסי's added line about timing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba raises an objection:
"And that one takes and eats,
phrases.notes: He is quoting a ברייתא that starts with our משנה's words and then adds more.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei forbids [it].
Rabbi Yosei said: When [is it forbidden]?
When his vow came before his making it ownerless."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי יוסי using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יוסי's reason is הפקר כמתנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under הפקר כמתנה, the order of vow and הפקר should not matter. But the ברייתא limits רבי יוסי's ban to when the vow came first, which points to a different reason.
